correctness.rationale: The normalized Gaussian ambiguity has squared magnitude exp{−πr²(cosh s+sinh s cos(2φ−2αj))}. Every term decreases radially, reducing closed-disk minimum to boundary. For equal weights, angular sum over three cube-root phases has strictly decreasing dependence on cos(3·2φ) by negative third derivative/divided differences; minima occur at six axes. Averaging responses at those axes bounds any unequal allocation, strictly unless wj=1/3 for s>0. Scalar Lc(u)=−√(c²+u²)+log[(e^−u+2e^{u/2})/3] has derivative v(u)−u/√(c²+u²); threshold map C(u)=u√(v^-2−1) strictly rises from 2 to infinity using (y−1)(y+2)>(1+2y)log y. Hence c≤2 unique zero squeeze (weights arbitrary), c>2 unique positive squeeze/equal weights. Series yields cubic onset and s→(log3)/2 with stated decay. Independently checked c=0.7,2,2.01,2.5,4,10 and exact derivative identity; numerical points do not prove uniqueness.
